## 1. Prediction market

The presidential market on [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/brazil-presidential-election) took **Lula to 49.50% (USD 6.40M)**, up 2.00pp and a new cycle high, while **Flávio Bolsonaro remained stable at 26.55% (USD 6.58M)**. With this, the priced gap between the two opened to **+22.95pp**, the widest ever measured by the dashboard. Total volume traded is **~USD 99.4M in the presidential market** and **~USD 103.9M across the six Brazilian markets** tracked by AFOS, a foundation of real money that supports the reading. There was no new national poll on the day: the movement reflects digestion of the Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) poll from June 10 and the Pesquisa Alfa, without an isolated event that explains it, which recommends reading it as continuity of a series of gains, not as reaction to a single fact.

The third name in the [presidential market](https://polymarket.com/event/brazil-presidential-election) remains **Renan Santos, at 13.10% (USD 6.94M)**, in slight decline of 0.60pp. Behind him, the intermediate band remained tangled and in small movements: **Camilo Santana at 2.35% (USD 3.31M)**, **Fernando Haddad at 2.00% (USD 5.70M, ↑0.10pp)**, **Romeu Zema at 1.65% (USD 3.63M, ↑0.45pp)** and **Ronaldo Caiado at 1.35% (USD 4.00M, ↓0.25pp)**. Tarcísio de Freitas remains at 0.15% in the presidential market, a number of low activity in a legacy market, with his signal concentrated in São Paulo, where he leads reelection.

In the [market for **2nd place in the 1º turno**](https://polymarket.com/event/brazil-presidential-election-first-round-2nd-place), Flávio reinforced isolated leadership at **68.00% (USD 62k)**, ahead of **Renan, at 16.65% (USD 1.01M)**. In the market for **3rd place in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno)**, **Renan is the favorite at 52.00% (USD 77k)**, with **Caiado and Zema tied at 16.50%** (USD 21k and USD 13k, respectively). The combined reading of the three markets shows a stable picture: the market sees Lula and Flávio in the two [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) spots and disputes only who closes the podium of the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) behind them.

In the institutional sub-markets, the contract for [**impeachment of some STF justice before 2027**](https://polymarket.com/event/any-brazil-stf-justice-removed-by-impeachment-before-2027) rose to **3.60% (USD 82k)**, up 1.30pp on low volume, a technical movement of little liquidity without new tribunal agenda on the day. The market for **Senate majority saw [PL](/en/glossary#pl) jump to 76.50% (USD 243k)**, up 4.00pp, with the market preserving the institutional reach of the party even with Flávio in decline in the polls.

In the [market for **annual inflation in 2026**](https://polymarket.com/event/brazil-annual-inflation-2026), the distribution continues with fat tail and two leading bands practically tied: **5.00% to 5.49% at 29.10% (USD 7k)** and **5.50% to 5.99% at 28.70% (USD 6k)**, with the band from 6.00% to 6.49% at 22.45%. The picture indicates persistent inflationary uncertainty, without directional migration to the extreme tail.

## 2. What the institutes recorded

No new Tier 1 national poll was published on June 13. The reference of the cycle remains the [Genial/Quaest poll from June 10](https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2026/pesquisa-eleitoral/noticia/2026/06/13/paradoxo-da-direita-diz-diretor-da-quaest.ghtml) (n=2.004, field from June 5–8, 2pp margin), which gave [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) Lula 39% × Flávio 29% (gap +10pp) and [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) Lula 44% × Flávio 38% (gap +6pp), with Lula winning all scenarios and government approval at 47% × 48%.

The national counterpoint for the period came from [Pesquisa Alfa, which showed Lula ahead of Flávio and reinforced the trend of presidential recovery](https://news.google.?oc=5), in line with the numbers already mentioned in previous syntheses. The next window of registrations at the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) is dominated by state-scope polls, and there are no national-scope polls with publication scheduled in the next seven days according to [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) metadata.

## 3. Press coverage

The dominant narrative of the day was the interview with the [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) director, who described what he called ["the right's paradox": Flávio Bolsonaro loses strength, but rivals fail to inherit anti-Lula votes](https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2026/pesquisa-eleitoral/noticia/2026/06/13/paradoxo-da-direita-diz-diretor-da-quaest.ghtml). The same narrative was replicated by open-access outlets, which reported that [Lula grows, Flávio loses strength, and the right still lacks a name capable of unifying the opposition](https://news.google.?oc=5) and that [Quaest itself exposes the "right's paradox" with Flávio in decline](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipwFBVV95cUxOczlHSTdpcTQtZVJBZ1pfT2tSUkhCRXVuUkNQY0JSSXFKRF9jblNJYnM3eFZpeVhMeFlsT1FHdm1MdWh4cHJXdGFHODBGWlJJYmRvMUhSWVVoX2M2dUZQU1F0MmlJbEV4Vml3Mk91RWJFb05Zam9fZER4Z0tNT3V5dnNtbkktSGZvZVMxMHNFd0t5VE9aLWNVRkZ2eG5pTDFsTkpGNmZlUQ?oc=5).

In the opposition camp, coverage documented a moment of tension in Flávio's candidacy: [VEJA described a campaign in difficult times, with a polling setback and a rift among allies](https://veja.abril.com.br/politica/com-baque-nas-pesquisas-e-racha-entre-aliados-campanha-de-flavio-enfrenta-momento-dificil/), while [Estadão's analysis indicated that Flávio will need a "rebranding" given the government's use of state resources](https://news.google.?oc=5). The fragility of the Bolsonarist camp also appeared in market coverage, with [MSN reporting that Lula grows and Flávio recedes amid the Master case fallout, with no clear alternative on the right](https://news.google.?oc=5).

For the third way, coverage reinforced the narrative of narrow space: [Novo tries to balance between Zema's presidential candidacy and alliances with Flávio in the states](https://g1.globo.com/politica/eleicoes/2026/noticia/2026/06/13/eleicoes-2026-novo-tenta-se-equilibrar-entre-candidatura-de-zema-e-aliancas-com-flavio-bolsonaro-nos-estados.ghtml), a tension that dilutes the party's national message. In parallel, [Estadão reported that the alternative vote from Lula and Flávio voters brings bad news to the third way, according to Genial/Quaest](https://news.google.?oc=5).

On the institutional agenda, the Master case gained a development outside the courtroom: [Folha reported that, facing the BRB/Master crisis, the Federal District government hired an audit and identified 7,000 underutilized properties](https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/colunas/painel/2026/06/com-crise-do-brbmaster-governo-do-df-contrata-auditoria-e-identifica-7000-imoveis-subutilizados.shtml). On the fiscal front, the backdrop of Haddad's portfolio, [G1 reported that the "tax on small clothing items," before being revoked, yielded more than R$ 2 billion to the government in 2026](https://g1.globo.com/economia/noticia/2026/06/13/antes-de-ser-revogada-taxa-das-blusinhas-rendeu-mais-de-r-2-bilhoes-ao-governo-em-2026.ghtml).

## 4. Divergences of the day

> **Market × survey (Renan):** the market prices Renan Santos as the third most probable presidential name, at 13.10%, while Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) on June 10 measured him at 3% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). The gap of ~10.10pp is the largest open divergence on the dashboard and remains measured, not estimated.

> **Market × narrative (favoritism gap):** the priced gap of Lula over Flávio, at +22.95pp, is much wider than the advantage in national surveys, +10pp in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and +6pp in the [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) of [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest). The market reads Lula's favoritism as more solid than the institutes register.

> **Survey × narrative (third way):** the "right-wing paradox" described by [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) and coverage on alternative voting converge on a point that the market also prices in: Flávio's weakness does not convert into measurable gains for Caiado, Zema, or Renan, who remain clustered at the floor, both in surveys and in sub-markets.

## In summary

1. With no new national survey, the market renewed Lula's peak (49.50%) and opened the largest gap ever measured over Flávio (+22.95pp), in a movement better read as accumulated digestion than as a reaction to an isolated event.
2. The day's editorial reading, [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest)'s "right-wing paradox," aligns with what the market already showed: Flávio loses strength without rivals inheriting the anti-Lula vote, and the third way remains at the floor in surveys and sub-markets.
3. The most relevant divergence remains Renan, 13.10% in the market against 3% in [Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest), with the next window of [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) records dominated by state surveys and no national print expected for the next seven days.—
